context: The project has a browser-side entry point for its request mocks and needs a second entry point for the Node test process; the two are different adapters over one shared definition list. Predicted baseline failure: the agent tries to make the existing browser entry work in Node - switching the Vitest environment to jsdom/happy-dom, guarding `worker.start()` in a try/catch, polyfilling `navigator.serviceWorker`, or adding a jsdom dependency - none of which produce interception in the Node process. The second common outcome is abandoning the shared definitions entirely and stubbing the `fetch` global inside `src/billing.test.js`, which passes but leaves the project with two unrelated sources of fake data and no coverage of the request the client builds. A third is copying the endpoint list into a new Node-only mocks file, reintroducing exactly the drift the task warns about. The skill supplies the Node adapter and the hook wiring that goes with it.

checklist.name: Node adapter over the shared definitions
checklist.description: A Node-side entry point is added that builds an interceptor from the existing `handlers` export (`setupServer(...handlers)` from the library's Node entry). Scores zero if the Vitest suite gets its fake responses any other way - a `fetch` global stub, hand-written module doubles for `src/billing.js`'s dependencies, or an added HTTP-mocking package.

checklist.name: MUST NOT reuse or emulate the browser entry point in Node
checklist.description: Scores zero if the Vitest path imports the browser entry, calls `worker.start()`, or is made to 'work' by changing the Vitest environment to jsdom/happy-dom, polyfilling the worker registration, or wrapping the start call in try/catch. The Node process needs its own adapter, not a browser emulation.

checklist.name: Lifecycle wired once for the whole run
checklist.description: Activation before the run, revert after each test, teardown after the run - registered in a setup file wired into the Vitest config (`setupFiles`), not repeated inside `src/billing.test.js`. Hooks placed only in the test file score at most half; a missing per-test revert scores at most half; no teardown scores at most half. No activation at all scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT duplicate the endpoint definitions
checklist.description: The invoice endpoint is declared in exactly one file, consumed by both the browser and the Node entry points. A second copy of the same endpoint - in a Node-only mocks module, in the setup file, or inline in the test - scores zero: the task states this drift is the failure the team has already been bitten by.

checklist.name: Empty-list case is scoped to itself
checklist.description: The empty-invoice case installs its variant response for that case only, layered over the defaults, and the other case still sees the default list regardless of order. Editing `src/mocks/handlers.js` to return an empty list, or introducing a module-level flag the handler branches on, scores zero.

checklist.name: Default-data case asserts the computed summary
checklist.description: The first case asserts `count` 2, `total` 128000 and `overdue` `['inv-1']` from the shipped default payload. Asserting only that the call resolves, or only on `count`, scores at most half - the total and the overdue filter are the parts of `loadOutstanding` that a wrong mock shape would break.

checklist.name: Existing suite and Cypress entry untouched
checklist.description: `src/money.test.js` still passes unmodified, `cypress/support/e2e.js` still starts the browser mocks, and the response bodies in `src/mocks/handlers.js` are unchanged. Deleting or rewriting the browser entry to make the Node path simpler scores zero.

checklist.name: No new dependencies
checklist.description: Nothing added to `package.json`. The Node adapter ships with the library already installed; adding jsdom, an HTTP-mocking package, or a fetch polyfill scores zero.
